extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Popular Science Monthly (educated general public, scientists, and book/exhibition readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative principles used in magazine literary notices and editorials to judge books, exhibitions, educational institutions, and scholarly reports. Emphasizes textual fidelity, pedagogical priority, exhibition value, authorial qualities, evidence, and methodological rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use primary texts when judging theoretical works
rubrics_metrics.description: An examination should be of the works in which the theory is professedly expounded rather than in a volume which disavows all attempt to formulate the principles of the science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not judge an author's theory by side discussions or works that were not intended to present the systematic treatment; example: Dr. Porter undertakes to judge Spencer's 'Theory of Sociology' by analyzing a book that does not contain it — an anti-pattern to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensational criticism and misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that are extensive, incomplete, or comprehensive in method invite misconception and sensational criticism, which makes misrepresentation easy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should correct false impressions rather than exploit an author's incompleteness for sensational effect; be more discriminating and avoid misconstruing large, fragmentary bodies of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize practical, life-preserving knowledge in curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: The knowledge that conduces to self-preservation (e.g., hygiene, physiology) should be taught first and thoroughly in colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If textbooks are inadequate or teachers incompetent, replace them; pedagogical priority should favor knowledge that averts preventable catastrophes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess representativeness of institutional spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.description: When a public figure speaks before a state institution and customary exercises are suspended in their behalf, their statements may be taken as representing the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be discriminating about whose statements to trust, but recognize that invited institutional speakers often speak as representatives and their factual claims warrant scrutiny and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition value: novelty, variety, and instructiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairs and exhibitions should present sufficient new and interesting objects to give novelty and pleasure; they should be instructive and offer favorable opportunities for observing and comparing articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate exhibitions for variety, ability to familiarize the public with high standards of excellence, and for stimulating further improvement; international exhibitions especially can stimulate communities to apply greater intelligence to the arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair governance: judicious conduct and discretion in awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The judicious conduct of the society and the discretion with which awards have been bestowed are important factors in an exhibition's standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should weigh the fairness and consistency of award decisions as part of an exhibition's merit and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial expertise and prior reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's previous work and familiarity with subject-matter (scientific knowledge, special studies) commend a book and indicate authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the author's background, special studies, and up-to-date knowledge (e.g., geology, botany, zoology) when judging the trustworthiness and value of a work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and temper: non-polemical, moderate presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A desirable work is written in excellent temper and is free from asperity or polemic; it enforces views by illustration rather than contentious argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor books that avoid harsh polemics, maintain a temperate tone, and appeal by harmonizing ideas (e.g., science and faith) instead of antagonizing potential readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and clarity balanced with restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear and pleasing writing with vividness and occasional poetic feeling is positive, but undue fervor and over-elaboration of style are faults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prose for lucidity and engaging expression while noting when rhetorical excess detracts from substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of scientific results and respect for scientific practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Good treatment looks upon science not as an enemy but as a handmaid of other perspectives, accepts advanced views, and avoids disparagement of scientific men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how accurately and respectfully scientific findings are integrated into broader arguments; avoid works that misrepresent or denigrate scientific disciplines or practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy/reform proposals must be robust against worst-case scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: A system or political reform must be judged by its ability to meet the worst cases, not merely when applied by best actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test proposals for vulnerability to partisan abuse or perverse incentives; historical plausibility and safeguards against hostile exploitation are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of historical evidence and rigorous argumentation in proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should review relevant history (e.g., English and American examples) to support their positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the sufficiency and interpretation of historical evidence and whether it genuinely supports the proposed remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook criterion: comprehensive yet concise exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful manual presents a brief exposition of a complete science — describing known phenomena and indicating current theories and problems of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge textbooks by their ability to cover essentials succinctly while pointing readers to deeper works; valuable as a stepping-stone to larger treatises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook organization and topic selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of treatment and omission of recondite subjects may be appropriate when aiming for an introductory manual (e.g., external morphology, anatomy chapters, physiology, classification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the organizational choices serve the intended audience and pedagogical aims; omission of very recondite topics can be a deliberate, appropriate editorial choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and usefulness of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous, attractive, and well-drawn illustrations that are helpful to understanding the text are a substantive merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh both quantity and the pedagogical helpfulness of figures; good illustrations support comprehension especially in scientific manuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological reporting: terse description and avoidance of speculative theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions should be terse and to the point; authors ought not to invent theories about race or symbolic meaning where not warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor works that present reliable descriptive data and resist overinterpretation; provide precise illustrations and avoid reading symbolism into every design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical utility and audience fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Handy, clear, and concise books that suit the needs of the local or target audience (e.g., naturalists of New England coast) are valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the book meets practical requirements of intended readers and whether its scope matches local or specialist interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration attribution and scholarly citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and draughtsmen should give authorities for drawings and otherwise cite sources for illustrative material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of attribution for drawings or data is a scholarly shortcoming; insist on citations and authorities for illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production quality: binding, printing, and physical presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Handsome binding and printing and overall production values contribute to a book's merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider physical presentation (paper, typography, binding) as part of the review, especially for works intended for field or classroom use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnographic methodology: standardized data collection and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather ethnographic information by enlisting many reliable observers and sending a circular clearly setting forth the kind of information desired and precautions for reliable observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the methodological rigor — use of trained correspondents, standardized questions, and explicit instructions to minimize careless observation and observer bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnographic comprehensiveness and solicitation of cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to cover a wide ground (care of the lifeless body, burial methods, ceremonies, gifts, superstitions, mourning practices) and solicit cooperation to make final publications complete and valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the project collects a sufficiently broad set of topics and whether it proactively seeks contributions from observers to build a comprehensive, trustworthy dataset.
